title: Silverline Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Silverline Health onboarding to Redwood. Discussed project scope, success metrics, environment choices (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), SSO/KMS requirements, initial pilot plan, and next steps including access to sandbox, security docs, and scheduling a technical deep dive/benchmark. Agreed timeline: 6-week pilot with canary rollout to 5% traffic, target latency SLOs, and security review by end of week.
action_items: Maya Chen | Share onboarding guide + sandbox credentials | 2027-08-02
Samir Patel | Schedule deep-dive bench session and request sample traffic/profile | 2027-08-05
Jill Torres | Provide project plan & weekly check-in cadence | 2027-08-03
Liam O'Connor | Send network diagrams and VPC requirements | 2027-08-04
Priya Nair | Confirm KMS/HSM provider and encryption requirements | 2027-08-06
next_steps: Redwood to send onboarding pack and sandbox creds
Schedule technical deep dive with SEs for inference benchmarking
Customer to share sample request volumes and SLO targets
Security review: customer to share SOC2 report and Redwood to share security docs
Agree pilot start date and success metrics
meeting_header: Date: 2027-08-01 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes | Location: Zoom
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everyone, thanks for joining. this is the Silverline onboarding kickoff. um i'm Maya, your AE. 
[00:08] Maya Chen: Quick intro from our side, Samir's our SE, Jill's your CSM, we'll be running the pilot and the onboarding.
[00:15] Liam O'Connor: Hey Maya, thanks. I'm Liam, CTO at Silverline. we'll probably jump into env details — i have Priya from infra and Rachel from data.
[00:22] Priya Nair: hi all. Priya, DevOps lead. small correction, we're considering a VPC private deployment because of PHI concerns but open to dedicated if quicker.
[00:30] Dr. Rachel Kim: Rachel here; main goals are to get embeddings flow for search and generation for triage notes, keep latency under 300ms p50 on short prompts, and ensure auditability.
[00:42] Samir Patel: thanks, Rachel. that's helpful. ok, we'll talk through the hosting options — Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). each has tradeoffs for latency, cost, and data isolation.
[00:53] Maya Chen: to set expectations, most customers in regulated spaces start with a dedicated pool or private. Dedicated gives predictability and isolation without full private setup. Private is for strict network controls and customer-managed keys.
[01:07] Evan Brooks: what's the typical lead time for private?
[01:10] Samir Patel: usually 3-6 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS integration. Dedicated can be provisioned faster, often within a week if capacity's available.
[01:19] Liam O'Connor: okay, budget wise we have procurement windows at the end of the month, but security sign-off is the gating factor. can you provide SOC2 docs and KMS/HSM integration notes?
[01:30] Jill Torres: yes we'll share the security packet. Redwood has SOC2 Type II, plus SAML/SSO integrations and KMS examples. we'll attach audit log formats as part of the onboarding pack.
[01:41] Priya Nair: good — specifically we need guidance on how the KV cache and prefix caching work with private networks, and whether any egress is needed.
[01:50] Samir Patel: good question. for Private VPC we support private peering and the runtime keeps KV cache local; there should be zero egress for inference calls if you route through the private control plane. minor control plane traffic to our management endpoint can be routed over the peering link — we'll document specifics.
[02:05] Dr. Rachel Kim: and about quantization — we want to know if smaller models affect clinical quality for triage prompts. any suggestions?
[02:12] Samir Patel: yes, we have quantization profiles and model recommendations in Redwood Optimize. for sensitive outputs we recommend testing both fp16 and 4-bit profiles; we can run A/B tests in the pilot to measure latency/cost vs quality regressions.
[02:26] Maya Chen: on the pilot: what's success? Rachel?
[02:30] Dr. Rachel Kim: success is 1) embeddings similarity within 95% of our current baseline for retrieval tasks, 2) generation quality acceptable for triage notes (we'll supply prompt sets and evals), 3) throughput to handle 150 reqs/min peak, and 4) security sign-off.
[02:44] Maya Chen: great. we'll capture that as the success criteria.
[02:47] Evan Brooks: timeline — can we do a 6-week pilot? week 1: sandbox and onboarding; week 2: run small benchmarks; week 3-5: full pilot and A/B tests; week 6: review and decision.
[03:00] Jill Torres: that aligns with our standard plan. we'll own weekly check-ins.
[03:04] Priya Nair: on networking, we need a sample diagram from Redwood to show to our infra security team.
[03:09] Samir Patel: we'll send a network diagram and the VPC peering checklist. also note we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or external HSM — what's your provider?
[03:21] Priya Nair: we use AWS KMS but may need HSM for certain keys.
[03:26] Samir Patel: fine. we can support that — we'll include the integration steps.
[03:29] Liam O'Connor: what about SSO? we use Okta.
[03:32] Jill Torres: we have a SAML SSO flow and SCIM for provisioning. we'll send the SSO guide and sample metadata.
[03:38] Dr. Rachel Kim: any concerns on PII/PHI retention? we need logs to be retained for 7 years for audits.
[03:45] Maya Chen: retention policies are configurable; for Private deployments you can fully control logs, and for Dedicated we persist audit logs and can export to customer S3 with retention lifecycle rules. we'll verify retention windows.
[03:58] Evan Brooks: on pricing — we need high level for Dedicated vs Private.
[04:03] Maya Chen: we'll share a pricing spreadsheet; Dedicated is committed monthly pricing plus per-token stamping for overages. Private has licensing + support and higher fixed cost but lower per-token for large throughput.
[04:14] Liam O'Connor: competitors — we looked at Anthropic and OpenAI API for quick MVP but prefer a solution that scales to private deployment.
[04:22] Maya Chen: understood. we'll include comparative notes.
[04:26] Samir Patel: for the bench session, pls share a sample of your traffic distribution and some representative prompts, we'll run latency and quality benchmarks on our side.
[04:36] Dr. Rachel Kim: we'll anonymize and share sample prompts and some eval sets.
[04:40] Priya N'air: slight audio glitch earlier, sorry.
[04:44] Maya Chen: no worries. any blockers from your side today?
[04:47] Liam O'Connor: just internal procurement timing and need to get security to review the docs. once we have the network diagram and KMS details we'll spin up the review.
[04:56] Jill Torres: we'll target sending docs tomorrow and scheduling weekly check-ins starting next Tuesday.
[05:02] Maya Chen: ok let's recap actions and owners. Jill will send project plan and cadence; Samir will schedule bench deep-dive; I'll send onboarding pack and sandbox creds; Silverline will provide traffic & SLOs, network diagrams, and KMS details.
[05:19] Evan Brooks: sounds good. one quick question about fallbacks — if Dedicated capacity is hit, how does Redwood handle graceful degradation?
[05:26] Samir Patel: we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies. you can configure a policy to fall back to a smaller model or a hosted fallback region; we also support canary rollouts and rate limiting to protect SLAs.
[05:39] Dr. Rachel Kim: and traceability — can we tag requests with internal IDs for audit?
[05:44] Samir Patel: yes request-level traces and tags are supported; traces flow into Redwood Console and can be exported for your observability tools.
[05:53] Liam O'Connor: perfect. thanks.
[05:55] Maya Chen: thank you all. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. appreciate the time.
[06:00] [meeting ends]
